title: The Village People Episode
summary: Josh and Chuck (with Jerry in the booth) cover the Village People: the disco act conceived by Jacques Morali and Henri Belolo after they saw gay Greenwich Village bar patrons dressed as American macho stereotypes; the group's formation with Victor Willis, Felipe Rose, Glenn Hughes, Alex Briley, David Hodo and Randy Jones; hits "San Francisco (You Got Me)", "Macho Man" and "YMCA" (including the YMCA dance and its later baseball-stadium tradition); "In the Navy" and its Navy recruitment video; the 1980 film Can't Stop the Music and the Razzies; Victor Willis's departure, legal fight and control of the name; whether the group was a "gay group"; and the deaths of Glenn Hughes, Morali and Belolo. The episode ends with live tour announcements and a listener-mail tease.
topics: Stuff You Should Know live tour

segments.title: Live tour promo
segments.summary: Hosts promote Stuff You Should Know Live tour dates in Medford, DC and NYC and point to ticket sources.
topics: Stuff You Should Know Live tour

segments.title: Opening banter and Village People fandom
segments.summary: Hosts open the show, recall childhood fandom of the Village People, and compare the group to other bands known by names that aren't their real names, like Hall and Oates.

segments.title: Morali and Belolo's background
segments.summary: Hosts describe producers Jacques Morali and Henri Belolo, their separate early careers, and their formation of Can't Stop Productions.

segments.title: Brazil and the Richie Family
segments.summary: The producers' first project updated the song Brazil with the Richie Family as a disco hit; it was proto-disco and was nominated for a 1976 Grammy, losing to The Hustle.

segments.title: Origin of the Village People concept
segments.summary: In Greenwich Village, the producers saw men in gay bars dressed as American macho stereotypes, including Felipe Rose as an American Indian character, and conceived the group.

segments.title: Forming the group and first album
segments.summary: Victor Willis sang on the first single San Francisco (You Got Me); an ad sought gay singers and dancers with mustaches, and members including Glenn Hughes, Alex Briley, David Hodo and Randy Jones were recruited.

segments.title: Recruitment and original lineup
segments.summary: Hosts describe the casting call responses and the original six-member lineup and their roles, then take a break.

segments.title: American Bandstand debut
segments.summary: The group made its American Bandstand debut in December 1977; hosts also discuss parenthetical song titles of the era.

segments.title: Macho Man and gay liberation lyrics
segments.summary: The 1978 album Macho Man and its title single are discussed, including the lyrics that shift from body worship to a call for gay liberation and the song's significance.

segments.title: Touring and fan reactions
segments.summary: The group toured heavily, unusual for disco acts; a Washington Post account describes hostile audiences and Glenn Hughes's experience with fans; their two-year peak is noted.

segments.title: Was Village People a gay group? and YMCA
segments.summary: Members' and journalists' statements about whether the group was gay are discussed; Victor Willis was straight but wrote the lyrics. YMCA came from Randy Jones's visits to the Manhattan YMCA, with a lyric about the world seeming 'so jive'.

segments.title: YMCA dance and baseball tradition
segments.summary: The arm-gesture dance for YMCA is explained as an audience-sparked move, the YMCA trademark issue is recounted, and the Yankees grounds crew YMCA tradition from 1996 is described.

segments.title: In the Navy and Navy recruitment video
segments.summary: The 1979 single In the Navy and its lyrics are discussed; the Navy used the song for recruitment and the music video was shot aboard the USS Reasoner.

segments.title: Can't Stop the Music movie and Razzies
segments.summary: The 1980 film Can't Stop the Music, starring Steve Guttenberg, is described as a fictionalized Village People story and as inspiring the Razzie Awards; its Australian box office is mentioned.

segments.title: Victor Willis departure, lawsuit and later lineups
segments.summary: Willis left in 1979 amid legal and drug problems; Ray Simpson led later touring lineups; Willis won a court case giving him control of the name, and later he formed his own version; a 2008 Hollywood Walk of Fame ceremony is described; hosts reflect on the original members.

segments.title: Status of original members and favorite characters
segments.summary: Hosts check which members are alive: Glenn Hughes died of lung cancer, Morali and Belolo are deceased, and Randy Jones released a 2017 dance single; hosts share which costume character they liked.

segments.title: Tour dates and listener mail teaser
segments.summary: Hosts mention upcoming Village People tour dates and transition to listener mail.

segments.title: Listener mail intro and live show announcement
segments.summary: Hosts announce that they skipped listener mail for a live show announcement, covering kid-friendliness and tour dates in Medford, DC, NYC, Chicago, Minneapolis, Indianapolis, Durham and Atlanta.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts ask for ticket purchases via the website or link tree and invite listener mail to the show's email address.
